name: Kok-Moynok Canyons
dist: Territory of the town of Balykchy
near: Kok-Moynok-2 village (Kok-Moynok Ekinchi) — the access road goes through it; Balykchy — 11–12.5 km.
elev: 1,500–1,700 m above sea level (Asiamixtravel); elevation gain from the parking lot to the upper points — up to 170 m (hiking.kg).
short: Kok-Moynok is a labyrinth of red-and-yellow sandstone canyons and “towers” above the Chu River at the exit of the Boom Gorge, 165 km from Bishkek and 12 km from Balykchy.
desc: The Kok-Moynok Canyons (“green hollow/blue isthmus”) lie on the right bank of the Chu between the Boom Gorge and the Orto-Tokoy Reservoir, beyond the village of Kok-Moynok-2. It is a network of dry erosion gullies up to 200 m deep in red and yellow sandstones and clays: narrow corridors, the “Rocket” rock in the middle of the main canyon, and viewpoint hills overlooking the Chu. The place can be seen in 2–3 hours: from the parking lot to the main formations it is about 1.3 km and up to 170 m of gain. In dry weather a passenger car can reach it, but after rain the dirt road along the river turns to mud and the dry channels may fill with water. There is no infrastructure; locals charge a token fee for driving in (50–300 som according to reviews), and in the off-season it is sometimes free.
guide: Turn off the highway at the fuel station before Balykchy towards Kochkor, cross the bridge over the Chu and follow the dirt road along the river through Kok-Moynok-2 — another 5–7 km and the parking lot is in front of you. From there it is 20–30 minutes up the wide channel to a “city” of towers: find the “Rocket” rock and climb any hill — from there you can see the turquoise Chu and the layered walls. Go through the narrow corridors with a partner, not alone, and only if no rain is expected: a downpour turns these channels into a torrent within minutes. The best light is in the evening, when the sun hits the red walls from the side; in summer by day it is scorching with no shade. This is not Konorchek: to reach it you have to walk 5 km from the highway, whereas here you can drive almost right up — which is why Kok-Moynok makes a handy stop on the way to Issyk-Kul or Song-Kol.
see: Narrow erosion passages, sandstone towers and viewpoint hills; the “Rocket” rock; a panorama of the Chu River and the Boom Gorge; wild horses on the approaches; sunset light on the red walls.
skip: You're already going to Konorchek or Skazka (Fairy Tale) — the geology is similar, and Kok-Moynok is smaller. It's raining or rain is expected — the channels are dangerous and the dirt road turns to mud. A summer midday with children — hot and no shade.
diff: Easy: 2/5 on foot on the hiking.kg scale, up to 1.3 km from the parking lot and up to 170 m of gain; the drive in is 3/5 because of the dirt road. Suitable for families with children; be careful in the narrow corridors — the rock crumbles.
when: May–October (Asiamixtravel); spring and autumn are more comfortable than summer (hot by day). In winter it is usually accessible — there is little snow. Don't go in the rain or right after it.
hours: Open area, open 24 hours; no ticket offices, though locals may charge a fee on the approach (see “Entry cost”).
daytime: The second half of the day and sunset (the “golden hour”) — side light on the red walls, with no backlight when walking up the channel; sunrise is also good but colder.
how: From Bishkek along the A-365 highway through the Boom Gorge ~165 km (2.5–3 h); before Balykchy, turn onto the Kochkor/Naryn road, turn off at the Bishkek Petroleum fuel station, cross the bridge over the Chu and then follow 4–7 km of dirt road along the river through the village of Kok-Moynok-2 to the parking lot at the canyon (5 minutes after the village there is a fork — go left). From Balykchy 12.5 km (25–35 min), from Kochkor ~45 km (~1 h). Public transport does not run to the canyon.
needcar: Yes: 4–7 km of dirt road from the highway; you can walk from the highway, but it is long and dusty. A passenger car can make it in dry weather.
self: Yes: the route from the parking lot along the channel is obvious, no permits are needed; take an offline map (Maps.me/2GIS), water and closed shoes; don't go into the narrow side branches alone.
roadtype: Paved road along the A-365 to the turn-off; then a dirt road along the Chu through Kok-Moynok-2 (4–7 km), in places right at the water; in dry weather passable by a passenger car with care (low ground clearance — be careful), after rain only high clearance/4x4. In the canyon — sand and rocks, unmarked trails.
traveltime: Bishkek — parking lot 2 h 45 min — 3 h (165 km); Balykchy — 25–35 min; Kochkor — ~1 h. The walking part is up to 1.3 km and up to 1.5 h one way; 2–3 h for the whole visit.
stay: There is no accommodation on site (camping is possible, but there is no infrastructure). The nearest: hotels and guesthouses in Balykchy (12 km), CBT and guesthouses in Kochkor (45 km), guest houses on the west shore of Issyk-Kul. A landmark on the highway is the roadside café Ak-Jol. 2025–2026 prices are not confirmed.
net: There is coverage in the villages of Kok-Moynok and by the highway; inside the canyons the signal drops out behind the walls (a general pattern in the Boom Gorge; there are no reports by operator). Download offline maps.
entry: There is no official fee. According to 2GIS reviews (2024–2026), locals on the approach/parking lot charge 50–300 som per person; an April 2024 blog says free; hiking.kg warns of a possible fee at the main parking lot without giving an amount. Ask what the fee is for.
transfer: Taxi from Bishkek with waiting ~6,000 som/car (July 2024); Asiamixtravel jeep tour $324 per group of up to 4 people with breakfast (2025); Bishkek — Balykchy train 40–60 som (summer 2024).
bring: Water (1–1.5 L/person), a hat and sun protection (no shade), closed shoes with a non-slip sole, a charged phone with offline maps, a windbreaker, a snack, wet wipes; cash in small notes for a possible fee.
warn: Heavy rain quickly fills the dry channels with water — in a downpour turn back immediately; don't enter the narrow gullies alone. The rocks crumble — don't climb the walls. In summer it is extremely hot by day; in 2024 tours were cancelled because of the heat. After rain the dirt road by the river turns to mud. An unofficial fee on the approach is possible (50–300 som). Respect the wild horses — don't approach them.
food: On the highway near Balykchy — roadside cafés (lagman, manty, shashlik; landmark Ak-Jol); in Balykchy — Issyk-Kul fish (smoked, fried), lunch ~1,500 som/person in local cafés according to a tour operator (2025). There is no food in the canyon.
reviews: 2GIS “Kok-Moynok Canyons”: 4.9/5, 255 ratings, 39 reviews (viewed 07.10.2026). Google Maps: the listing could not be matched (meta: ambiguous result). Pros: impressive red rocks “like in the USA”, deserted, accessible in an ordinary car, a beautiful sunset; cons: summer heat, no toilets or water, crumbling rocks, mud after rain, inconsistent fees for driving in (50–300 som).
p.sum: Kok-Moynok is the most accessible “red” canyon on the road from Bishkek to Issyk-Kul or Song-Kol (≈165 km, 2.5–3 h). Before Balykchy turn towards Kochkor at the fuel station, cross the bridge over the Chu and drive 4–7 km of dirt road through Kok-Moynok-2 to the parking lot. Then 1.3 km and up to 170 m of gain along the channel to the “Rocket” and the viewpoint hills, 2–3 h for everything. In dry weather a passenger car can make it too. Without a car — a day tour from Bishkek (too.kg from $195 per car, 2026) or a marshrutka (minibus)/train to Balykchy and a taxi. Locals sometimes charge 50–300 som on the approach: have small notes.

p.iti.1.title: On the way to Song-Kol/Naryn (2–3 days)
p.iti.1.plan: Day 1: Bishkek → Kok-Moynok (2 h) → Orto-Tokoy Reservoir → Kochkor (night with CBT). Day 2: Kochkor → Song-Kol (yurts).
p.iti.2.title: Combinations
p.iti.2.plan: Konorchek (turn-off from the Boom Gorge) + Kok-Moynok in one day; Kok-Moynok → Orto-Tokoy (20 km) → Kochkor; Kok-Moynok → Balykchy → south shore (Skazka, Mars).
p.season: March–April: cool, mud is possible. May–June: greenery by the river, comfortable. July–August: hot by day (tours were cancelled in 2024 because of the heat) — only morning/evening. September–October: the best light and temperature. November–February: little snow, usually accessible, cold and windy.
p.budget.economy: ≈1,000–2,000 som/person: Bishkek — Balykchy marshrutka 300 (×2) or a train from 150, taxi from Balykchy (by arrangement), a possible fee of 50–300, food 500.
p.budget.comfort: ≈4,000–8,000 som/person: too.kg tour from $195 per car, €282 (Putevka), taxi with waiting ≈6,000 som per car, lunch 1,000–1,500.
p.permits: Not needed. There is no official fee; an unofficial fee from locals on the approach of 50–300 som is possible.
p.access: With kids — yes (an easy 1.3 km trail; keep them close in the narrow passages). For older people — the lower part of the channel. With a wheelchair — no (sand, rocks). With a dog — possible, but it is hot.
